# Configure Okta as the SCIM identity provider

This topic describes how to configure Okta as the SCIM identity provider for <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name -->. After completing this configuration, <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> can accept SCIM provisioning requests from Okta for users and groups.

## Background

Okta provisions users and groups to <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:background-product -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:background-product --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:background-product -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:background-product --> using the SCIM protocol. Okta acts as the source of truth for user identities and group membership. When you assign a user or group to your <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:background-app -->Terraform Enterprise application<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:background-app --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:background-app -->custom HCP Terraform application<!-- END: TFC:only name:background-app --> in Okta, Okta pushes those changes to <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:background-product2 -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:background-product2 --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:background-product2 -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:background-product2 --> automatically.

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:background-matching -->
Terraform Enterprise matches incoming SCIM users to existing accounts by email address. When a match is found, the existing account becomes SCIM-managed. When no match is found, Terraform Enterprise creates a new account.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:background-matching -->
<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:background-matching -->
HCP Terraform matches incoming SCIM users to existing accounts by email address. When a match is found, the existing account becomes SCIM-managed. When no match is found, HCP Terraform creates a new organization-owned account. Okta group names become team names in HCP Terraform directly. There is no separate name mapping.

You cannot use the Terraform Cloud application from the Okta Integration Network gallery for SCIM. You must create a custom application to complete this configuration.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:background-matching -->

To configure Okta as the SCIM identity provider for <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:background-product3 -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:background-product3 --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:background-product3 -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:background-product3 -->:

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:background-steps -->
1. Configure the API integration in your existing Terraform Enterprise application in Okta.
1. Configure provisioning actions.
1. Configure group push.
1. Start provisioning and verify the setup.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:background-steps -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:background-steps -->
1. Create a custom application in Okta and configure SAML SSO on it.
1. Configure the API integration and configure the SCIM base URL and token.
1. Configure provisioning actions.
1. Configure group push.
1. Start provisioning and verify the setup.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:background-steps -->

## Requirements

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:requirements -->
Before you configure Okta as the SCIM identity provider, enable SCIM in Terraform Enterprise and generate a SCIM token. Refer to [Configure SCIM provisioning](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/configure) for instructions.

You must also have administrator permissions in Okta to configure SCIM provisioning. 

We strongly recommend creating a [non-SSO admin account for recovery](/terraform/enterprise/saml/troubleshooting#create-a-non-sso-admin-account-for-recovery) before enabling SCIM. This account allows you to log in and troubleshoot if there are issues with your SCIM or SAML configuration.

Before broad rollout, validate your Okta user identifier and attribute mappings with a small set of test users. During SCIM user creation, Terraform Enterprise links an existing Terraform Enterprise user by email address when the email matches.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:requirements -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:requirements -->
Before you configure Okta as the SCIM identity provider, enable SCIM in HCP Terraform and generate a SCIM token. You must also create a custom SAML application in Okta and have administrator permissions to configure SCIM provisioning. Refer to [Configure SCIM provisioning](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/configure) for instructions.

Before broad rollout, validate your Okta user identifier and attribute mappings with a small set of test users.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:requirements -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:custom-app -->
## Create a custom application

You must create a custom SAML application. You cannot use the existing Terraform Cloud application from the Okta Integration Network gallery.

1. From the Okta Admin Dashboard, navigate to **Applications** > **Applications**.
1. Click **Create App Integration**.
1. Select **SAML 2.0**.
1. Name the app and click **Next**.
1. Under **Configure SAML**, set the following values. The **Single sign-on URL** and **Audience URI** are temporary and will be replaced in a later step:
   - **Single sign-on URL**: `https://app.terraform.io/sso/saml/placeholder`
   - **Audience URI (SP Entity ID)**: `placeholder`
   - **Name ID format**: `EmailAddress`
   - **Application username**: `Okta username`
   - **Update application username on**: `Create and update`
1. Under **Feedback**, select **This is an internal app that we have created**.
1. Click **Finish**.
1. Copy the **Metadata URL** to use in the HCP Terraform configuration.
1. Configure SAML SSO in HCP Terraform for this new custom application by providing the Metadata URL you copied in the previous step. Follow the instructions in [Use single sign-on with Okta for HCP Terraform](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/single-sign-on/okta), up to and including the step to click **Enable**.
1. In the Okta application, update the following with the values from the HCP Terraform SSO configuration:
   - **Single sign-on URL**: use the Assertion Consumer URL from HCP Terraform
   - **Audience URI (SP Entity ID)**: use the Entity ID (Audience) from HCP Terraform
1. Verify the SSO configuration by clicking **Test**. If the test is successful, click **Enable**.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:custom-app -->

## Configure API integration

After SCIM is enabled, configure the SCIM connection in Okta.

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:api-integration -->
1. Log in to the Okta Admin Console.
1. Navigate to **Applications** > **Applications**.
1. Open your existing Terraform Enterprise application.
1. Click the **Provisioning** tab.
1. Click **Configure API Integration**.
1. Select the **Enable API integration** checkbox.
1. In the **SCIM connector base URL** field, enter the SCIM base URL from Terraform Enterprise:

   ```
   https://<TFE_HOSTNAME>/scim/v2
   ```

1. In the **Authentication Mode** section, select **HTTP Header**.
1. In the **Authorization** field, enter the SCIM token you created in Terraform Enterprise without the `Bearer` prefix. Okta automatically adds the `Bearer` prefix when making requests to Terraform Enterprise.
1. Configure the **Unique identifier field for users** according to your validated Okta provisioning setup.
1. Click **Test API Credentials** to verify the connection.
1. If the test succeeds, click **Save**.

The following table summarizes the required SCIM connection settings:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| SCIM connector base URL | `https://<TFE_HOSTNAME>/scim/v2` |
| Unique identifier field for users | Your validated Okta provisioning configuration |
| Authentication Mode | HTTP Header |
| Authorization | Your SCIM token value |
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:api-integration -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:api-integration -->
1. Sign in to the Okta Admin Console.
1. Navigate to **Applications** and open your custom HCP Terraform application.
1. On the **General** tab under **App Settings**, click **Edit** and select **SCIM** as **Provisioning**. After saving, a new **Provisioning** tab appears.
1. Click the **Provisioning** tab.
1. Click **Edit** for the SCIM Connection and complete the following fields:
   - **SCIM connector base URL**: Enter the base URL you copied from HCP Terraform. Refer to [Enable SCIM](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/configure#enable-scim) for more information.
   - **Unique identifier field for users**: Set to `email`.
   - **Supported provisioning actions**: Enable **Push New Users**, **Push Profile Updates**, and **Push Groups**.
   - **Authentication Mode**: Select **HTTP Header**.
   - **Authorization**: Enter the SCIM token you copied from HCP Terraform. Refer to [Enable SCIM](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/configure#enable-scim) for more information.
1. Click **Test Connector Configuration** to verify the configuration.
1. Click **Save**.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:api-integration -->

## Configure provisioning actions

After the API integration is verified, new settings appear under the **Provisioning** tab.

1. On the **Provisioning** tab, click **To App** in the left sidebar.
1. Click **Edit**.
1. Enable the following options:
   - **Create Users**: Allows Okta to create new users in <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name -->.
   - **Update User Attributes**: Allows Okta to update user attributes in <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name -->.
   - **Deactivate Users**: Allows Okta to deactivate users in <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> when they are unassigned or suspended in Okta.
1. Click **Save**.

## Configure group push

Complete the following steps to synchronize Okta groups:

1. Click the **Push Groups** tab.
1. Click **Push Groups** and select **Find groups by name** or **Find groups by rule**.
1. Search for and select the groups you want to push to Terraform Enterprise.
1. Click **Save**.

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:group-push-behavior -->
Okta creates corresponding SCIM groups in Terraform Enterprise for each pushed group. You can then link these SCIM groups to Terraform Enterprise teams. Refer to [Link SCIM groups to teams](/terraform/enterprise/scim/manage/team-mapping) for instructions.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:group-push-behavior -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:group-push-behavior -->
Okta creates corresponding teams in HCP Terraform for each pushed group. Okta group names become team names in HCP Terraform directly. When assigning groups, note the following factors:

- IdP group names become team names in HCP Terraform directly. There is no separate name mapping step.
- Group names must be fewer than 90 characters. 
- Nested group membership is not supported.
- HCP Terraform supports a maximum of 1,000 IdP groups and 1,000 members per group.

Refer to the following topics for more information about users and groups:

- [User lifecycle](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/users)
- [Group lifecycle](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/groups)

Before enabling SCIM, review existing team memberships. When an Okta group name matches an existing HCP Terraform team name, SCIM takes over that team and replaces its membership with the Okta group membership.

We recommend using separate groups for SSO access, which controls who can sign in, and SCIM team membership, which controls team assignments within HCP Terraform.

<!-- END: TFC:only name:group-push-behavior -->

## Start provisioning

Start with a small rollout to verify provisioning before broader adoption:

1. Click the **Assignments** tab in your <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> application.
1. Click **Assign** and select either **Assign to People** or **Assign to Groups**.
1. Select a test user or group to provision.
1. Click **Assign** for each selection, then click **Done**.

Initial provisioning may take longer than later updates, especially when provisioning many users or groups. Later provisioning runs only process subsequent changes.

When you assign users or groups:

- **Users**: Okta immediately provisions assigned users. Users can log in using SAML SSO after provisioning.
- **Groups**: If you configured group push, Okta creates the groups. Group membership is synchronized automatically.

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:deactivation-behavior -->
When Terraform Enterprise receives a SCIM user deactivation request, it suspends the user.

Assigning groups to the application does not automatically create team memberships in Terraform Enterprise. Link SCIM groups to Terraform Enterprise teams after the groups are provisioned. Refer to [Link SCIM groups to teams](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/manage/team-mapping).
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:deactivation-behavior -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:deactivation-behavior -->
When HCP Terraform receives a SCIM user deactivation request, it removes the user's access to HCP Terraform.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:deactivation-behavior -->

## Attribute mappings

The following tables show the Okta-to-SCIM mappings. The **Required** column reflects what <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> requires on incoming SCIM requests.

### Users

| Okta attribute | SCIM attribute | Required |
|----------------|----------------|----------|
| `userName` | `userName` | Yes |
| `emails` | `emails` | Yes |

<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:user-attr-note -->
Terraform Enterprise requires `userName` and at least one email value for each user. During user creation, Terraform Enterprise links existing users by email address when the email matches.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:user-attr-note -->

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:user-attr-note -->
HCP Terraform requires `userName` and at least one email value for each user. Set the **Unique identifier field for users** to `email`. During user creation, HCP Terraform links existing users by email address when the email matches.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:user-attr-note -->

### Groups

| Okta attribute | SCIM attribute | Required |
|----------------|----------------|----------|
| `displayName` | `displayName` | Yes |
| `members` | `members` | No |
| `externalId` | `externalId` | No |

## Test provisioning

After completing the configuration, verify that provisioning works correctly.

### Verify user provisioning

1. Assign a test user to the <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> application in Okta.
1. Wait a few moments for Okta to provision the user.
<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:verify-user -->
1. Log in to Terraform Enterprise as a site administrator.
1. Navigate to **Site Admin** > **Users**.
1. Verify that the test user appears in the user list.
1. Check that the user's email address matches the Okta user.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:verify-user -->
<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:verify-user -->
1. Navigate to your organization in HCP Terraform.
1. Verify that the test user appears with a status of **Synced - Provisioned**.
1. Test that the user can log in using SSO.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:verify-user -->

### Verify group provisioning

1. Push a test group from Okta.
<!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:verify-group -->
1. Log in to Terraform Enterprise as a site administrator.
1. Navigate to **Site Admin** > **SCIM**.
1. Verify that the group appears in the SCIM groups list.
1. Link the group to a Terraform Enterprise team and verify membership synchronization.
<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:verify-group -->
<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:verify-group -->
1. Navigate to **Teams** in your HCP Terraform organization settings.
1. Verify that the group appears as a team.
1. Confirm team membership reflects the Okta group membership.
<!-- END: TFC:only name:verify-group -->

### Verify user deactivation

1. Unassign a test user from the application in Okta.
1. Wait a few moments for Okta to deactivate the user.
1. Log in to <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> and verify that the user is deactivated.

## Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with Okta SCIM provisioning, use the following guidance to diagnose and resolve common problems.

### Authentication failures

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| `401 Unauthorized` error | Invalid or expired SCIM token | Create a new SCIM token and update the Okta configuration. |
| Test API Credentials fails | Incorrect base URL or token | Verify the SCIM base URL format and ensure the token value is correct. |
| Connection timeout | Network or firewall issues | Verify that Okta can reach your <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> instance. Check firewall rules and network connectivity. |

### User provisioning failures

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| Users not created | Incorrect user identifier or attribute mapping | Review the Okta user identifier and attribute mappings, then test with a single user before broad rollout. |
| Duplicate user errors | Existing user or SCIM identity conflicts with the incoming Okta user | If the email matches an existing user, <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> links that user to SCIM. <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->If the conflict involves another unique attribute, refer to [Troubleshoot SCIM provisioning](/terraform/enterprise/scim/troubleshooting#users-not-syncing).<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --> |
| User attributes not updating | Update User Attributes not enabled | Enable **Update User Attributes** in the Okta provisioning settings. |

### Group provisioning failures

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| Groups not appearing | Push Groups not configured | Configure group push in Okta and select the groups to push. |
| Group membership not syncing | <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:group-sync-cause -->SCIM group not linked to a team<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:group-sync-cause --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:group-sync-cause -->Groups not yet pushed to HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:group-sync-cause --> | <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:group-sync-solution -->Link the SCIM group to a Terraform Enterprise team. Refer to [Link SCIM groups to teams](/terraform/enterprise/scim/manage/team-mapping).<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:group-sync-solution --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:group-sync-solution -->Confirm group push is configured and the group has been pushed to HCP Terraform.<!-- END: TFC:only name:group-sync-solution --> |
| Large group operations timeout | Group exceeds size limits | Split large groups into smaller groups. The maximum is 1,000 members per group. |

### Rate limiting

Okta may encounter rate limits when provisioning large numbers of users or groups. If you see `429 Too Many Requests` errors, it's because <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> temporarily rate-limits SCIM requests when request volume is too high. Review the Okta provisioning logs, wait for provisioning to continue, and refer to [Troubleshoot SCIM provisioning](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/troubleshooting) if the condition persists.

### View provisioning logs in Okta

To view detailed provisioning logs and error messages:

1. In the Okta Admin Console, navigate to your <!-- BEGIN: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name -->Terraform Enterprise<!-- END: TFEnterprise:only name:product-name --><!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:product-name -->HCP Terraform<!-- END: TFC:only name:product-name --> application.
1. Click the **Provisioning** tab.
1. Click **View Logs** to see recent provisioning events.
1. Filter by status to find failed operations.

For additional troubleshooting guidance, refer to [Troubleshoot SCIM provisioning](/terraform/cloud-docs/scim/troubleshooting).
